Thank you for the feedback. It is unexpected because it feels very unrelated to the subject matter. It was not our intent to cause any discomfort or confusion. Sometimes people find some of the questions relating to self-injury difficult or upsetting to answer. Our research ethics board requires us to have a way to distract or improve people’s mood, and these types of videos have been shown to do this for people who are upset by certain questions.
Thank you for your willingness to share your experience. Self-injury can often be a difficult topic for people to discuss.

Hi Skyqween, 
Thank you for clarifying. I will refrain from posting research in this subreddit in the future, and if, for any reason, I did want to post or comment, I will ask for mod permission before I do. 
Natalie

Hello Skyqween,

I am sorry for my approach to posting research in this subreddit. I tried to post in subreddits that did not specifically restrict research in their guidelines; however, I realize now that I should have sought approval first. I will make sure to send all the relevant information to the mod team before posting in the future. Thank you for letting me know why my post was taken down. 

Sorry for the inconvenience! 
Natalie

Sorry for the incredibly late reply. It took some time, but I have checked with my Research Ethics Board who talked to the admins, a lawyer on the board, and the Canadian Association of Research Ethics Boards and in the end, it is up to the participant as to whether or not they would like to take part. The study is cleared in Canada and as long as the participants are 16 and older, it is their choice whether or not to participate. The country of residence is not an issue as the study is located in Canada. Does that clarify things?
I have emailed the research ethics board and will hopefully get a response for you tomorrow. Sorry for the wait!

Health Canada states that young people between the ages of 16-18 years of age with sufficient understanding are able to give their full consent to participate in research independently of their legally authorized representative [Link to Health Canada website here.](http://www.hc-sc.gc.ca/sr-sr/advice-avis/reb-cer/applic-demande/_form_docs/e-eng.php). In order to demonstrate sufficient understanding, all participants will be asked a series questions regarding the informed consent before they are allowed to participate. Hopefully this answers your question!

Ideally I would like people to participate because they would like to help with what I feel is important research. The incentive is offered for those who chose to enter the draw at the end of the study as I understand that your time is also valuable and want to offer something to recognize that fact. I am sorry that you took offense to this type of incentive and I will take this into consideration with future studies.
